<cite ref="Shabbat 73b:1">Sabb. 73ᵇ</cite> <he>מ׳ למה לי</he> why does the Mishnah state the number (39)?; <cite ref="Keritot 2b:1">Kerith. 2ᵇ</cite>; a. fr.—
Bekh. 60ᵃ bot. הואיל ואיתיה במ׳ פרסאה וכ׳ because it occurs in the Persian (?) system of counting that they call ten one.—
<cite ref="Sanhedrin 36a:6">Snh. 36ᵃ</cite>; <cite ref="Gittin 59a:1">Gitt. 59ᵃ</cite> <he>אנא הואי במ׳</he> I was one of the voters in the school of Rabbi, and with me they commenced.

<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Sanhedrin 1:2:13">Y. Snh. I, 18ᶜ</cite> top [read:] <he>אין אנא סלקית ממ׳ וכ׳</he> whether or not I was counted in (to make up the required number); a. fr.—Pl. <he>מִנְיָנַיָּא</he>, <he>מִנְיָינֵי</he>, <cite ref="M01393"><he>מִי׳</he></cite>.
<cite ref="Onkelos Numbers 1:44">Targ. Num. I, 44</cite>; a. fr.—Gitt. l. c.; <he>כולהו מִנְיָנַיְיהוּ וכ׳</he> in all their ballots they began their vote from the side benches (with the juniors).—
<cite ref="Shabbat 66b:19">Sabb. 66ᵇ</cite> <he>כל מ׳ וכ׳</he> all incantations which are repeated several times, must contain the name of the patient’s mother; a. e.
